key_insight: Adaptive Algorithmic Control (A2C) shows that reallocating finite computational resources adaptively can improve quantum optimization results by equalizing cumulative computational hardness, not physical time.
engineering_relevance: This provides a software-level control strategy that can boost quantum simulation and optimization performance without requiring better hardware, making resource scheduling an important design lever for near-term quantum systems.
method: Uses a State-Proxy Equalization theorem to determine the optimal adaptive allocation policy.
Infers computational hardness directly from the evolving quantum state, avoiding explicit many-body spectrum reconstruction.
Dynamically adjusts resource allocation during computation to minimize a proxy-error functional.
evidence_signal: Across exact simulations, supercomputer runs, and IBM hardware experiments on problems up to 156 qubits, A2C improved low-energy sampling probabilities by 22% to over 100,000% at matched circuit depths and measurement budgets.
watch_item: The approach depends on reliable state-derived proxy estimates, so performance may be sensitive to noise, approximation quality, and how well the proxy tracks the true target objective.
paper_title: Beyond Hardware: Adaptive Algorithmic Control by State-Proxy Equalization
